skill.displayName: Pet Body Condition Score 3D Analysis | 宠物体态3D评分（BCS）

llm.summary: The skill’s pet video analysis purpose is real, but it also silently creates or reuses cloud identity context and stores authentication tokens locally, so it needs Review before install.

dimensions.detail: Sending user-provided media or URLs to the analysis backend fits the purpose, but environment/workspace detection plus remote silent login and account-scoped report retrieval are under-scoped for the described user-facing task.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No separate permission manifest was present, while the skill requires network access, local file reads, local writes to workspace data, shell execution of Python modules, and runtime dependencies.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs automatic attachment saving, cloud history lookup, and hidden internal identity handling; the identity parameter is suppressed in the CLI and users are told not to be asked about it.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The common DAO creates a workspace SQLite database with sys_user records and token/open_token fields, and RequestUtil persists tokens returned from /sys/phoneLogin without a clear retention or deletion control.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Core BCS video/URL analysis via a remote API is coherent with the stated purpose, and history-report lookup is documented, but the account-backed history/export path and shared common API utilities broaden the skill beyond one-off observation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending pet videos or URLs, an internally generated user identifier, and report-history requests to the publisher’s cloud services. Ask the publisher to document account creation, token storage, retention/deletion behavior, and how to remove local data such as the workspace SQLite database before using it with sensitive media.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The need for network and local media handling is expected, but the missing explicit permission/consent surface is material because identity, local storage, and token persistence are also used.
[SDI-1] expected: History listing and report export are documented in SKILL.md and implemented in the CLI/API path, so this is disclosed, though broader than a single current-video analysis.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The local sys_user model stores profile fields and token/open_token values; that persistence is not proportionate to an observation-only pet analysis skill without clearer user controls.
[SQP-1] expected: The pet media trigger matches the purpose, but there is no explicit confirmation step before local files or URLs are sent to backend services.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Local attachment handling and API use are described, but hidden open-id handling, suppressed identity parameters, and remote identity/account flows are not adequately surfaced to users.
[E1] unexpected: RequestUtil posts openId, mobile, and source to /sys/phoneLogin and stores returned tokens, which is materially broader than simply submitting pet media for BCS analysis.
[AST7] expected: The dynamic getattr filter helpers are generic local DAO code; I did not find an externally exposed arbitrary-filter path in the reviewed workflow, so this is a secondary code-quality risk rather than the verdict driver.
